back: in fact / really. 'Actualmente' = currently / at the moment
example: Actually, I've changed my mind. / Currently, I work in Madrid.

back: in the end, after a long time. 'Eventualmente' = possibly / if necessary; 'trabajo eventual' = temporary work
example: We eventually found the hotel.

back: help. 'Asistir a' = attend
example: Our support team will assist you with the set-up. / Over 300 people attended the conference.

back: awkward, self-conscious (weaker than 'ashamed'). 'Embarazada' = pregnant
example: I was so embarrassed when I called my boss by the wrong name. / She's pregnant with her second child.

back: reasonable, practical. 'Sensible' = sensitive
example: That's a sensible decision. / She's very sensitive.

back: understand, become aware of. 'Realizar' = carry out, do
example: I didn't realise the meeting had been moved. / The researchers carried out a survey.

back: act as if something is true. 'Pretender' = intend, aim
example: He pretended not to see me. / What do you intend to do next?

back: biblioteca. 'Librería' = bookshop (UK) / bookstore (US)
example: You can borrow it from the library. / I bought it at a bookshop.

back: alfombra. 'Carpeta' = folder
example: I spilled coffee on the carpet. / Save it in this folder.

back: estreñido. 'Estar constipado' = to have a cold
example: I've got a cold, so I'll keep my camera off. (Never 'I'm constipated'!)

back: salida. 'Éxito' = success
example: The exit is at the back of the room. / The launch was a huge success.

back: tela. 'Fábrica' = factory
example: This fabric is 100% cotton. / She works in a car factory.

back: big. 'Largo' = long
example: We have a large number of clients in Mexico. / It was a very long meeting.

back: professional life. 'Carrera' (studies) = degree (AmE also: major). Not 'What career did you study?' -> 'What did you study?'
example: She's had a successful career in finance. / I did a degree in economics (AmE: I majored in economics).

back: go to (an event). 'Atender' = serve / deal with / pay attention
example: Will you be attending the meeting? / Could you deal with this customer?

back: a conversation about a topic. 'Discusión' (fight) = argument
example: We had a useful discussion about the budget. / They had a terrible argument.

back: showing understanding of someone's problems. 'Simpático' = nice / friendly
example: My manager was very sympathetic when my father was ill. / Her new boss is really nice.

back: subject. 'Tópico' = cliché / stereotype
example: Let's move on to the next topic. / That's just a cliché about Spaniards.

back: take away, get rid of. 'Remover' (soup) = stir - but 'remover de un cargo' = remove from office
example: Please remove my name from the list. / Stir the soup.

back: consejo (uncountable!). 'Aviso' = warning / notice
example: Can I give you some advice? / We received a notice about the changes.

back: abuse sexually - AVOID! 'Molestar' = bother / disturb / annoy
example: Sorry to bother you.

back: help/encourage. 'Soportar' = stand / put up with
example: Thanks for all your support. / I can't stand this noise.

back: a competition; (verb) formally challenge a decision. 'Contestar' = answer / reply
example: She won a photography contest. / We intend to contest the decision. / Please reply to my email.

back: a disagreement OR a line of reasoning. 'Argumento' (of a film) = plot
example: The plot of the film is confusing.

back: a talk at university. 'Lectura' = reading
example: The lecture starts at ten. / Reading is my favourite hobby.

back: an agreement where both sides give something up. 'Compromiso' = commitment
example: We reached a compromise on price. / Thanks for your commitment to the project.

back: suppose something is true. 'Asumir (responsabilidad / un cargo)' = take on / accept
example: I assumed you'd already left. / She took on the role of director.

back: 1,000,000,000 = 'mil millones'. 'Billón' = trillion
example: The company is worth $3 billion (tres mil millones).

back: list of points for a meeting. 'Agenda' (book) = diary (BrE) / planner (AmE)
example: What's on the agenda today? / Let me check my diary.

back: regular, reliable, coherent. 'Consistente' = solid, thick; well-founded
example: Her results are very consistent. / The sauce is quite thick.

back: present someone; bring in something new. 'Introducir' (a card, data) = insert / enter
example: Let me introduce my colleague. / Insert your card. / Enter your password.

back: ask for something forcefully. 'Demandar' = sue
example: They're demanding a refund. / They're suing the company.

back: start again after a pause. 'Resumir' = summarise (AmE résumé = CV)
example: The meeting will resume at 2. / Could you summarise the main points?

back: the way something is formed. 'Formación' = training / education / background
example: We offer training for new staff. / She has a background in law.

back: uncertainty / lack of belief. 'Tengo una duda' = I have a question
example: I have a quick question about the invoice.

back: show something is true. 'Probar' = try / test / taste
example: Can you prove it? / Try the new version. / Taste this.

back: achieve what you wanted. 'Suceder' = happen
example: She succeeded in closing the deal. / What happened?

back: a person hurt or killed. 'Casualidad' = coincidence / chance
example: What a coincidence! / We met by chance.

back: unusual, not common. 'Raro' = strange / weird / odd
example: That's a rare opportunity. / That's a bit strange.
